topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by connecting histopathology practicals to cellular changes and outlining the topics to be covered.

topics.label: Viral origins of oncogenes and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how studying transforming tumor viruses uncovered cellular proto-oncogenes and established experimental methods for assaying malignant cell transformation.

topics.label: Functional classes and molecular mechanisms of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the operational categories of cancer-associated genes and illustrate how specific mutations disrupt cell cycle controls to drive tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of genetic instability and multistep tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cellular failures in maintaining genome integrity produce genetic instability and accelerate the stepwise accumulation of mutations during cancer progression.

topics.label: Hereditary cancer predispositions and tumor maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how germline mutations predispose individuals to cancer and consider whether ongoing genetic instability is required to sustain malignancy.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and suggested reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture, offers supplementary reading recommendations, and previews the next lecture on cancer hallmarks.
